transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Fernandez (Redwood AE), Jonah Pryce (Redwood SE), Liam Carter (Horizon SRE), Aisha Khan (Horizon CTO), Diego Morales (Horizon Platform PM)

Summary:
- Short weekly pilot sync to look at the 48-hour run, tune autoscale thresholds, and agree an ops handoff for dedicated burst testing.

Topics:
- Observed latency and token throughput
- Autoscale policy tweaks (queue depth, CPU/GPU thresholds)
- Burst reserve plan and rehearsals
- Runbook ownership and rollback criteria

Action items and next steps are captured at the end.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do quick intro then go into the 48h readout. Jonah's got the numbers.
[00:20] Jonah: Yep, hi, uh, morning/afternoon. We ran the pilot traffic pattern you shared — synthetic traffic with a 20% spike window. overall throughput held up but we saw p95 climb at the 90th minute mark.
[00:38] Liam: Yeah that uptick matched what we saw, we had a couple of timeouts in the checkout microservice. Latencies spiked around 420ms p95, p50 stayed around 120ms which is within our target but the p95 is concerning.
[01:05] Jonah: Right — looks like the KV cache hit rate dropped during the sustained spike, I think the prefix caching wasn't applied for a subset of sessions. maybe our warmup wasn't long enough. also noticed batching was suboptimal when inbound concurrency peaked.
[01:35] Diego: Quick question — is the runtime using the quantized variant we discussed or the full fp16? that changes memory pressure and maybe the eviction behaviour.
[01:47] Jonah: We deployed q4f16 for cost reasons; that does reduce memory footprint but can increase per-token latency jitter with large sequences. could switch to fp16 for the rehearsal to see if p95 improves.
[02:12] Aisha: Our SLA goal is 150ms p50 and <350ms p95 for the checkout flow. We hit p50 but p95 exceed. We need deterministic behaviour before we go to production. also security wants audit logs retention — is that in the pilot?
[02:35] Maya: Yes, audit logs are on for the pilot — we have a 30-day retention in the console. we'll share the export process. on deterministic behaviour, Jonah suggested two levers: increase burst reserve and tune autoscale thresholds (queue depth and GPU util cutoffs).
[03:02] Jonah: For autoscale we currently scale up at GPU util 65% sustained for 30s and scale down at 30% for 90s. can tighten to 60%/20s scale up and 40%/60s scale down to be more aggressive on ramp. but that increases cost and possible oscillation.
[03:30] Liam: Happy to try more aggressive scale up for the Friday rehearsal but we want guardrails — how will fallback work if the Dedicated pool hits max capacity?
[03:44] Maya: Two fallback strategies: 1) route to hosted Canary model with lower-cost variant (higher latency, lower quality) 2) shed non-critical requests (e.g., background embeddings). We'll propose a policy that prefers fallback 2 for checkout-critical paths.
[04:08] Diego: Ok, we need explicit runbook steps — threshold numbers, who runs the mitigation, and how to roll back if fallback degrades experience.
[04:22] Jonah: Agreed. I'll draft a runbook with play-by-play: detection (p95>350ms sustained 2min), action A (spin 2x burst nodes), action B (activate hosted fallback route), post-mortem steps. Also include a quick command set for kube nets — kube delete? (transcription: kuber nets) 'kubectl drain' style ops for nodes.
[04:54] Aisha: Also confirm data residency — the hosted fallback must not send PII outside our region. can Redwood restrict fallback to same region or is it cross-region?
[05:10] Maya: We can restrict to region; can also restrict to redwood private tenancy for your account. We'll include restrictions in the policy and config.
[05:28] Jonah: on burst reserve sizing: based on the spike profile you gave (peak qps 1.8x baseline sustained for ~6 minutes), we recommend a 25% reserve of Dedicated capacity with a buffer to 40% during rehearsals. For Friday rehearsal recommend provisioning 2 extra 80GB GPUs (NVIDIA A10-ish) — that's our baseline suggestion.
[05:58] Liam: Do you have cost estimates for that reserve and the 2x extra nodes for 4 hours?
[06:06] Maya: I'll send a ballpark commit worksheet — but rough numbers: the 2x GPUs for 4 hours with network and infra overhead is approx $3.6k. If you want reserved burst, we can bake into the Dedicated commit with a discount.
[06:26] Diego: For autoscale we also want to ensure warm caches are populated before a test window. how do we pre-warm the KV cache and prefix caches? is there an API to replay sessions?
[06:40] Jonah: Yes, SE will provide a benchmark script that replays sample traffic and warms prefix caches and KV. It uses our replay tool and can be run from your CI or from Redwood infra. we'll share repo and run steps.
[06:58] Aisha: Perfect. For rehearsal, we want two runs: one cold start then warm. capture traces for both. we'll compare p50/p95 and KV hit rate.
[07:12] Jonah: Ok, I'll include that in the runbook and the script; will also include flags to force fp16 vs q4 variants for A/B testing.
[07:28] Liam: Another minor thing: when scale down occurs too quickly we saw request retries that amplified the problem. can you add jitter to scale down and a cooldown window for clients?
[07:44] Jonah: Yep — recommended cooldown of 90s and randomized backoff on the client side. we can add guidance in the runbook and sample client config.
[07:59] Maya: Quick commercial check — if the burst reserve becomes a regular requirement, we should talk commit sizing. i'll attach a worksheet after this call.
[08:10] Aisha: Sounds good. also security asked for SOC2 attestation and a whitepaper for encryption at rest with KMS — can you share?
[08:22] Maya: We'll share SOC2 cert and a security brief on KMS/HSM integration. will send through secure link.
[08:32] Diego: Do we need a PO for the rehearsal extras or can we use existing pilot credits?
[08:38] Maya: Short rehearsal we can absorb under pilot credits, but if you want reserved burst for longer we need a P.O. or a Dedicated addendum.
[08:50] Liam: Let's assume pilot credits for the Friday rehearsal. we'll confirm if we need a PO by Monday.
[08:58] Jonah: ok, next steps recap: I'll draft runbook and share autoscale configs; Maya will share pricing and security artifacts; Liam will run smoke tests and upload results; we schedule rehearsal for Friday 2026-03-13 22:00 UTC.
[09:20] Aisha: One last ask — can we instrument a single synthetic user journey that exercises the worst-case path so we can validate end-to-end?
[09:30] Jonah: Yes, the benchmark script includes a checkout heavy path. we'll send details.
[09:38] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts. Meeting adjourned.
